Skills BluffB (18/+26), Concentration (18/+26), Craft (construction) (18/+23), Fly (18/+30), Knowledge (lore) (18/+22), Perception (18/+26), Planar Sense (18/+26), Spellcraft (18/+25), Stealth (18/+15)
Environment any
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary, pair, or storm (3–10)
Treasure NPC gear (max. 21,800)
Sucking Wind (Sp) Bind (0 level) + Cascade Spell (inertia; +1 level) + Augment Spell (staggered; +2 levels) + Reach Spell (close to line of sight; +3 levels) + Mass Effect Spell (1/3 levels; +2 levels) + Concentration Spell (standard; +1 level) = 9th level; up to 6 creatures within 4.5 miles are entangled and staggered while polyp concentrates +1 rd./level.
Wind Blast (Sp) Energy mace (0 level) + Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to burst; +2 levels) + Explosive Spell (+1 level) = 4th level; damage 10d6 bludgeoning and thrown from 20’r. blast area.

A flying polyp is a physical being, but composed of material strangely unlike the flesh of most living creatures. The material seems to fade in and out of visibility, almost at random, at points becoming transparent enough that the nauseating inner workings of the thing's body are laid bare. Although the polyp feels moist and damp to the touch, what might serve as blood in other creatures behaves more like strange vortices of wind within a flying polyp's body. When wounded, its damaged flesh does not bleed so much as gust.
A flying polyp's association with wind goes far beyond the strange storms that surge through what pass as veins and arteries in its massive body. These creatures have a remarkable ability to control the air around them. They do not wield tools or weapons as a rule, instead using their mastery of the winds themselves to wage war and build their grim cities, scouring high, windowless towers and chambers out of basalt with precise blasts of sand-laden wind.
Although flying polyps display some of the features of other sentient races, particularly in their habit of building cities (although these towering settlements usually incorporate architectural features that most other races find awkward and unsettling), in other areas they seem strangely primitive or uninterested. They are as aberrant in mind and philosophy as they are in physical form. For example, they seem to have neither a name for their own race, nor a language to call their own. Their cities, while bewildering in their vast scale, seem to serve little purpose other than to unnerve, for flying polyps do not engage in trade or politics or other social constructs.
The primary exception to this, to the detriment of other creatures unfortunate enough to dwell in regions claimed by flying polyps, is war. Flying polyps excel at genocide, using their mastery over wind to scour clean entire cities and civilizations when they come upon them. Some among their kind can even travel to other planets by bringing with them a sizable sphere of purloined wind to carry them aloft and sustain them, and with this power they lead armies from planet to planet as necessary, relentlessly tracking their chosen enemies across worlds. Every so often, flying polyps encounter a race that is their equal in war, and on some worlds, they still endure the humiliation of these ancient defeats after being imprisoned in extensive underground chambers where they are cut off from the outside world. Yet flying polyps are long-lived, and should unforeseen tectonic events create new exits to their prison chambers, they emerge with unabated fury to seek revenge against the enemies who humiliated them.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+4 Str, +0 Dex, +2 Con, +3 Int, -2 Wis, +2 Cha; racial +2 Dex); racial feats: lightning reflexes, tremorsense; racial traits: open minded, skill focus (Fly); aberrant gifts: amorphous, partial invisibility, frightful presence.

sections.heading: Star Vampire
sections.text:
The blood never reached the floor. It stopped in midair as the laughter ceased, and a loathsome sucking noise took its place… A reddish glow filled the corner by the window—a bloody glow. Slowly but surely the dim outlines of a Presence came into view; the blood-filled outlines of that unseen shambler from the stars. It was red and dripping; an immensity of pulsing, moving jelly; a scarlet blob with myriad tentacular trunks that waved and waved. There were suckers on the tips of the appendages, and these were opening and closing with ghoulish lust.
―Robert Bloch, “The Shambler from the Stars” (1935)

An unnatural tittering issues forth from the fanged maw of this floating mass of talon-tipped tentacles, all as red as freshly spilled blood. Tangled masses of writhing feelers surrounding toothy maws, star vampires can extend three long tentacles tipped with talons to lacerate foes, allowing the aberrations to drink the blood from the air with thousands of tiny feeding tendrils. Naturally invisible, star vampires expose their offensive shapes when they feed, for the blood they gorge upon infuses their bodies with a glistening crimson hue. A star vampire is approximately 10 feet in diameter, yet weighs a mere 300 pounds.
Star VampirePF110	Cr 6
Giant, obah-blessedDu136 aberrant paragon 3
CE Large aberration [mythos]
Init +3;	Senses darkvision 60 ft., scent blood; Perception +19
Languages Aklo
AC 17, touch 12, flat-footed 14; miss chance 50%
(-1 size, +1 Dex, +2 dodge, +5 natural)
hp 76 (9 HD; LW 38/HW 19); blood healing 5
Immune precision effects (amorphous)
Fort +7, Ref +4, Int +8, Will +8
Weaknesses bleed effects
Spd 20 ft., fly 40 ft.
Melee 4 tentacles +10 (1d6+5 plus grab) and
bite +8 (1d8+2)
Face 5 ft. x 5 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Base Atk +6; CMB +11 (grapple +14); CMD 20
Special Atks constrict (2d6+7 plus 1d6 Con)
Attributes Str 20, Dex 12, Con 18, Int 9, Wis 16,    Cha 17
Feats Crippling Strike, Dodge, Feat Mastery (crippling strike), Improved GrappleB, MultiattackB, Skirmish, Vital Strike
Skills Fly (9/+12), Perception (9/+19), Stealth (9/+9)
Environment any (space)
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary, pair, or clot (3–8)
Treasure incidental
Blood Healing (Ex) Whenever a star vampire starts its turn within 10 feet of a creature suffering a bleed effect or Con damage (other than itself or another star vampire), it heals 5 hp and loses its invisibility (see below).
Partial Invisibility (Su) A star vampire is invisible in its natural state, although the eerie tittering it constantly emits makes locating it easier than normal—treat	a star vampire as if it were in combat or speaking for the purposes of Perception checks against it. When a star vampire feeds on blood (either as a result of a successful blood drain attack or by gaining the benefit of its blood healing), it becomes visible until it takes 2 consecutive rounds of bleed damage or 10 minutes pass after it last fed.
Scent Blood (Ex) A star vampire has the scent ability against all living creatures that have blood, and it gains a +10 circumstance bonus on Perception checks against creatures currently taking bleed damage.

Weakness to Bleed Effects (Ex) When subjected to a bleed effect, a star vampire suffers wracking pain that leaves it sickened as long as the bleed effect persists. Consumed blood drains rapidly from a star vampire’s body when it is affected by a bleed effect, and after 2 consecutive rounds of bleed damage, a star vampire that had become visible after drinking blood becomes invisible again.
The bulk of these creatures drift through the vastness of the Dark Tapestry, but without the starflight ability, thousands or even millions of years can pass before one manages to find a planet where it can descend to feed. Once a star vampire arrives on a planet, it adopts the new world as its personal feeding ground and very rarely, if ever, returns to space.
It is far more common for a star vampire to show up on a world after being conjured from the depths of space via certain rare spells or rituals. Many of these rites are deliberately ambiguous promises of the aid of a powerful spirit from the depths of space—designed to serve up the unsuspecting occultist as a hungry star vampire’s inaugural meal on the new world.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+3 Str, +0 Dex, +2 Con, -2 Int, +4 Wis, +2 Cha); racial feats: darkvision, scent blood; racial traits: skill focus (Perception), +1; aberrant gifts: amorphous, flight, partial invisibility; accept weakness in exchange for blood healing.

A star vampire is approximately 10 feet in diameter, yet weighs a mere 300 pounds.

Star VampirePF110 Cr 6

Giant, obah-blessedDu136 aberrant paragon 3

CE Large aberration [mythos]

Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft., scent blood; Perception +19

Languages Aklo

AC 17, touch 12, flat-footed 14; miss chance 50%

(-1 size, +1 Dex, +2 dodge, +5 natural)

hp 76 (9 HD; LW 38/HW 19); blood healing 5

Immune precision effects (amorphous)

Fort +7, Ref +4, Int +8, Will +8

Weaknesses bleed effects

Spd 20 ft., fly 40 ft.

Melee 4 tentacles +10 (1d6+5 plus grab) and

bite +8 (1d8+2)

Face 5 ft. x 5 ft.; Reach 10 ft.

Base Atk +6; CMB +11 (grapple +14); CMD 20

Special Atks constrict (2d6+7 plus 1d6 Con)

Attributes Str 20, Dex 12, Con 18, Int 9, Wis 16, Cha 17

Feats Crippling Strike, Dodge, Feat Mastery (crippling strike), Improved GrappleB, MultiattackB, Skirmish, Vital Strike

Skills Fly (9/+12), Perception (9/+19), Stealth (9/+9)

Environment any (space)

Frequency very rare

Organization solitary, pair, or clot (3–8)

Treasure incidental

Blood Healing (Ex) Whenever a star vampire starts its turn within 10 feet of a creature suffering a bleed effect or Con damage (other than itself or another star vampire), it heals 5 hp and loses its invisibility (see below).

Partial Invisibility (Su) A star vampire is invisible in its natural state, although the eerie tittering it constantly emits makes locating it easier than normal—treat a star vampire as if it were in combat or speaking for the purposes of Perception checks against it. When a star vampire feeds on blood (either as a result of a successful blood drain attack or by gaining the benefit of its blood healing), it becomes visible until it takes 2 consecutive rounds of bleed damage or 10 minutes pass after it last fed.

Scent Blood (Ex) A star vampire has the scent ability against all living creatures that have blood, and it gains a +10 circumstance bonus on Perception checks against creatures currently taking bleed damage.

Weakness to Bleed Effects (Ex) When subjected to a bleed effect, a star vampire suffers wracking pain that leaves it sickened as long as the bleed effect persists. Consumed blood drains rapidly from a star vampire’s body when it is affected by a bleed effect, and after 2 consecutive rounds of bleed damage, a star vampire that had become visible after drinking blood becomes invisible again.

The bulk of these creatures drift through the vastness of the Dark Tapestry, but without the starflight ability, thousands or even millions of years can pass before one manages to find a planet where it can descend to feed. Once a star vampire arrives on a planet, it adopts the new world as its personal feeding ground and very rarely, if ever, returns to space.

It is far more common for a star vampire to show up on a world after being conjured from the depths of space via certain rare spells or rituals. Many of these rites are deliberately ambiguous promises of the aid of a powerful spirit from the depths of space—designed to serve up the unsuspecting occultist as a hungry star vampire’s inaugural meal on the new world.

Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+3 Str, +0 Dex, +2 Con, -2 Int, +4 Wis, +2 Cha); racial feats: darkvision, scent blood; racial traits: skill focus (Perception), +1; aberrant gifts: amorphous, flight, partial invisibility; accept weakness in exchange for blood healing.

sections.heading: Gnoph-Keh
sections.text:
...the sharp horn of the Gnoph-keh, the hairy myth-thing of the Greenland ice, that walked sometimes on two legs, sometimes on four, and sometimes on six.
―H.P. Lovecraft and Hazel Heald,
"The Horror in the Museum"
A vortex of freezing wind swirls around this six-legged, bearlike monstrosity. A single horn protrudes from its snarling face. With its dirty white fur and great scarlet claws, a gnoph-keh looks at first glance somewhat like a great polar bear as it erupts from cover beneath a snowbank and lopes to attack. Only those who survive its fierce onslaught have the leisure to notice its abnormalities: it has too many legs (six, not four); its claws are not bloodstained, but naturally black and red; and it has a wicked 2-foot-long horn in the center of its muzzle. Worse of all, the wicked intelligence in its piercing red eyes could never be found in any simple animal, no matter how fierce.

Giant, advanced, awakened, icyAB, obah-blessedDu136 animal paragon 3
CE Large magical beast [cold, mythos]
Init +3; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, snow sight; Perception +10
Aura cold 20 ft. (5d6, DC 19)
Languages Aklo
AC 24, touch 12, flat-footed 21
(-1 size, +3 Dex, +12 natural)
hp 92 (8 HD; LW 34/HW 17); Diehard
Immune cold
Fort +15, Ref +11, Int +12, Will +11
Weakness vulnerability to fire
Spd 40 ft.; ice walking
Melee gore +12 (1d8+7/19-20/x3 plus 1d6 cold)
and 4 claws +12 (1d6+7 plus 1d6 cold and grab)
Face 5 ft. x 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Base Atk +6; CMB +13 (grapple +16); CMD 26
Special Atks bleeding critical (1d4), charge +14 (2d8+20/19-20/x2 plus 1d6 cold and grab), constrict (2d6+10 plus 1d6 cold and 1d4 bleed)

1/day—summon blizzard (see below; DC 19)

SQ favored terrain (arctic) +4
Feats Bleeding Strike, Improved GrappleB, Improved Multiattack, MultiattackB, Rapid StrikeB, Slowing StrikeB, Spirited Charge, Vital Strike

Skills Athletics (4/+14), Concentration (8/+16), Endurance (8/+16), Perception (8/+15), Stealth (8/+14; +18 in arctic), Survival (4/+11; +15 in arctic)
Environment any
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary, pair, or gathering (3–8)
Treasure standard
Summon Blizzard (Su) Wisp (0 level) + Cascade Spell (ray of frost; +1 level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 40’r.; +1 level) + Extend Spell (inst. to 1 min./level; +2 levels) + Residual Spell (+1 level) + Restricted Spell (cold subtype; -1 level) + Reduce Spell (15d6 to 5d6; -2 levels) = 4th level; 5d6 cold/rd. and obscures vision in 40’r., which counts as difficult terrain.
The gnoph-keh is a six-legged horned creature vaguely akin to a polar bear in shape and outline, yet possessed of a cruel and creative intellect that elevates it from the rank of wild beast to murderous warmonger. Covered with a dense pelt of shaggy white fur, the gnoph-keh is equally at home walking on two, four, or six legs. The creature prefers to travel on all six when using its powerful charge or running, but rears up on its hind legs in combat to bring its four front claws to bear on its foes. With the gnoph-keh’s ability to call up and direct powerful blizzards matched to its ability to move and see in such conditions without any disadvantage, the creature is rightfully feared in the frozen realms where it dwells.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: NPC (-4 Con, +4 Wis); racial feats: ferocity, natural armor, resistance; racial traits: fast, open minded; special attacks: augmented critical, skill focus (Stealth). For a CR 11 elder gnoph-kehPF46, increase racial HD by 6; its blizzard is 80 feet in radius and also staggers those within.

sections.heading: Great Race of Yith
sections.text:
They seemed to be enormous iridescent cones, about ten feet high and ten feet wide at the base, and made up of some ridgy, scaly, semi-elastic matter. From their apexes projected four flexible, cylindrical members, each a foot thick, and of a ridgy substance like that of the cones themselves. These members were sometimes contracted almost to nothing, and sometimes extended to any distance up to about ten feet. Terminating two of them were enormous claws or nippers. At the end of a third were four red, trumpet-like appendages. The fourth terminated in an irregular yellowish globe some two feet in diameter and having three great dark eyes ranged along its central circumference. Surmounting this head were four slender grey stalks bearing flower-like appendages, whilst from its nether side dangled eight greenish antennae or tentacles. The great base of the central cone was fringed with a rubbery, grey substance which moved the whole entity through expansion and contraction.
―H.P. Lovecraft, “The Shadow Out of Time” (1936)
Great RacePB3 	Cr 9
Giant, advanced, half-axiomatic aberrant paragon 2
LN Large aberration [mythos]
Init +2; Senses alertness +4 (DC 36), blindsense 45 ft., darkvision 60 ft., Planar Sense 120 ft., uncanny dodge, improved uncanny dodge, detect hostile intent; Perception +22
Languages Aklo, Common, Yithian, Tsath-Yo, 11 other languages; telepathy 120 ft.
AC 24, touch 10, flat-footed 22
(-1 size, +2 Dex, +6 insight, +7 natural)

fast healing 5
Immune [debilitation], sleep

resolve, evasive will

Ranged lightning projector +14 touch (14d6)
Face 5 ft. x 5 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Base Atk +10; CMB +17; CMD 28
Psi-Like Abilities (ML 14th)
1/day—mind switchSRD (DC 21), lesser programmed amnesiaCA (DC 22; no implanting of memories), extended time hopSRD (DC 23), astral projection (self only)
3/day—modify memory (DC 19), hold monster (5d4 Dex, DC 20)
At will—detect chaos, detect thoughts (DC 17), magic circle against chaos

Attributes Str 22, Dex 15, Con 19, Int 25, Wis 21, Cha 21
Feats Blind-Fight, Canny Defense, Feat Mastery (blind-fight), Great Fortitude, Improved Critical (claws), Iron Will, Weapon Specialization (claws)
Skills Athletics (14/+23), Bluff (14/+22), Concentration (14/+29), Craft (technological devices) (14/+22), Endurance (1/+8), Heal (14/+19), Knowledge (linguistics, lore, the planes) (14/+24), Perception (14/+22), Perform (acting) (14/+19), Planar Sense (13/+21), Spellcraft (14/+24)
Environment any
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary, band (2–9), enclave (10–100)
Treasure NPC gear (mojo 8,400; max. 10,050): lightning projector (see below)
Lightning Projection (Sp) Electric arc (0 level) + Amplify Spell (+1 level) + Reach Spell (close to long; +1 level) + Irresistible Spell (+2 levels) = 4th level; damage cap 15d6 electricity. 4th level x CL 7th x 500 (use-activated) x 3/5 (3/day uses) = 8,400.
Untold eons ago, the yithians inhabited a dying world. To escape their doomed planet, they cast their minds through time and space, eventually coming to rest in the strange, alien bodies they possess today. While these strange beings now reside in a distant galaxy, the yithians make use of their ability to astrally project to explore other planets, eager to find new worlds to explore.
When a yithian arrives upon a new world, it often swaps minds with the creatures it encounters there so as to experience that world as if it were a native. Those who spend time in a yithian's body rarely tell of the strange times they have experienced, for yithians guard themselves well, and leave those they use in this manner amnesiacs who remember the truth only as fragmentary nightmares.
As befits their alignment, the great race maintains a fascistic, socialistic society in which individual freedoms are minimized in order to maintain social cohesion. They are often in fierce competition with the flying polyps and other aberrant beings. If not destroyed by violence, a yithian can live for 4,000-5,000 years.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+2 Str, +0 Dex, -2 Con, +4 Int, +2 Wis, +3 Cha); racial feats: additional traits, darkvision; racial traits: agile climber, skill focus (Concentration), improved natural attack, open minded; aberrant gifts: fast healing, immunity. Rumor has it that exceptionally old members of the Great RaceCoC are of Huge size, and even greater intelligence, but physically less robust; apply the Giant simple template again, reduce racial HD by 3, and apply the NPC stat array (-6 Dex, +6 Int).

sections.heading: Hooded Harbibger
sections.text:
This creature resembles a mummified humanoid swathed in filthy, sallow rags. Its stooped posture and ragged coverings make its height hard to judge. Its arms appear abnormally long, or perhaps dislocated and hanging freely. A hood of the same jaundiced fabric obscures its face.
Hooded HarbingerPF112	Cr 9
Advanced, variant tanar’ri aberrant paragon 2
CE Medium aberration [chaotic, evil, mythos]
Init +8; Senses darkvision 60 ft., planar sense 20 ft., see invisibility; Perception +21
Aura profane reek 5 ft. (see below; DC 21), unnatural aura
Languages Aklo, Common; telepathy 120 ft.
AC 25, touch 21, flat-footed 17
(+4 Dex, +4 dodge, +3 insight, +4 natural)
hp 161 (17 HD; LW 80/HW 40); DR 10/lawful
Immune negative energy, poison
Resist acid 10, cold 10, fire 10; SR 30
Fort +9, Ref +8, Int +7, Will +13; improved evasion, improved insight, improved resolve
Spd 30 ft.
Melee 2 slams +20 (1d4+12/19-20) or
bloodless touch +16 touch (see below)
Base Atk +12; CMB +26; CMD 40
Supernatural Abilities (ML 17th)
10/day—channel negative energy (1d6, DC 18)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 17th)
1/day—extended freedom of movement, manifest Yellow Sign (see below; DC 22), plane shift, augmented (8d4) mass hold person (DC 24), terrible visage (see below; DC 25)
3/day—dispel magic, tongues, fiendish teleport*, confusion (DC 21), kindred summon monster IV (1 Advanced keeper of the Yellow Sign, 60%), prophetic utterance (see below)
At will—bloodless touch (see below; DC 18), detect law, hold person (DC 19), silence (DC 19)
Attributes Str 26, Dex 18, Con 21, Int 16, Wis 13, Cha 24
Feats Command UndeadB (56 CR), Deep Intuition, Dodge, Improved Critical, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Permanent Spell (aura), Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics (17/+21), Athletics (17/+25), Bluff (17/+27), Concentration (17/+27), Escape Artist (17/+21), Knowledge (planes) (17/+23), Perception (17/+21), Planar Sense (17/+21), Stealth (17/+24)

Environment any land
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary (plus 1 possible Advanced Keeper of the Yellow Sign cohort and/or up to 50 CR worth of zombies)
Treasure standard
Bloodless Touch (Sp) Ray of entropy (1st level) + Cascade Spell (inertia; +1 level) + Augment Spell (staggered; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Cascade Spell (sickening touch; +1 level) + Lingering Evocation (+1 level) + Tenuous Spell (-1 level) + Restricted Spell (aberration; -1 level) + Reduce Spell (10d6 to 5d6; -1 level) = 1st level; melee touch deals 5d6 necrotic damage plus 2d6/rd. and staggered and sickened (save each round to end effects).
Death Throes (Sp) Bolt of force (2nd level) + Cascade Spell (alter senses; +1 level) + Augment Spell (blindness; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Shape Spell (target to burst; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r,; -1 level) = 4th level; damage cap 10d6 force plus blinded.
Manifest Yellow Sign (Sp) Ray of beguiling (1st level) + Cascade Spell (compel; +3 levels) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +2 levels) + Personal Spell (­1 level) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 120’r.; +3 levels) + Pattern Spell (visual; -1 level) + Restricted Spell (servant of Hastur; -1 level) = 5th level; onlookers within 120 ft. take a 1d6+15 penalty to Wisdom (confused at 1) and do not move or attempt to harm the caster in any way.
Profane Reek (Sp) Mind fog (5th level) + Reach Spell (long to touch; -2 levels) + Shape Spell (spread to emanation; +0 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.; -1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 hr./level; +2 levels) + Augment Spell (+10 to +15; +1 level) = 3rd level; those within 10 feet take a 1d6+15 penalty to Wis and Cha (Intuition half).
Prophetic Utterance (Sp) Doom (1st level) + Quickened Spell (+3 levels) + Interrupting Spell (+1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 10 min./level; +1 level) + Inexorable Spell (+3 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (just damaged caster; -2 levels) + Restricted Spell (aberration; -1 level) + Reduce Spell (panicked to shaken; -2 levels) = 4th level; as an immediate action, a hooded harbinger can cause a creature damaging it to be shaken for 170 min. (no save).
Terrible Visage (Sp) Damage attribute (Wis; 1st level) + Crippling Drain (+1 level) + Delay Spell (+1 level) + Pattern Spell (visual; -1 level) + Augment Spell (+2d4; +3 levels) + Cascade Spell [(bolt of force; +2 levels) + Cascade Spell (alter senses; +1 level) + Augment Spell (blindness; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to personal; -1 level)] + Shape Spell (target to burst; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.; -1 level) + Delay Spell (+1 level) + Reduce Spell (25d6 to 15d6; -2 levels) = 8th level; onlookers of face (after slain) take 3d4 Wis drain, then body explodes for 15d6 force plus blinded in a 10’r. burst.
It is said that the Crawling Chaos is the messenger of the Great Old Ones, but whether this is by their command or his own whim is debatable. Regardless of why, the Great Old One known as Hastur sometimes instead relies on his hooded harbingers to relay messages to his far-flung cults and even to the High Priest Not To Be Described of mystery-shrouded Leng. These dread figures swathed in filthy yellow rags bear the whispered tidings of their Unnamed Lord. There are those who even speculate that the veiled priest of Leng is actually the greatest of the hooded harbingers, who gained some measure of autonomy—but the truth of this remains unknown. Thought to have originated in distant Carcosa by unthinkable means, hooded harbingers are exceedingly rare, and seldom is more than one encountered at a time.
Though tasked with the menial role of messengers, hooded harbingers take their charge very seriously. Infused with the hateful potency of their master, they are able to call upon many terrible powers in defense of their duties. When forced into combat, they prefer to trip opponents with the trailing ends of their ragged arm coverings and administer their bloodless touch to as many victims as possible. They always attempt to use plane shift to flee if in danger of imminent defeat.
Serving as messengers for Hastur, hooded harbingers receive the communications they deliver directly from the Great Old One via mental transmission. Upon receiving the message, the hooded harbinger twitches and shakes as if it were having a seizure. During this time they are particularly dangerous, because if they are attacked or distracted in any way, they fly into a furious rage and the offender risks attracting the attention of the King in Yellow.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: tanar’ri (+4 Str, +4 Dex, +4 Con, +2 Int, +2 Wis, +2 Cha), elite (+4 Str, +0 Dex, +2 Con, +0 Int, +0 Wis, +3 Cha), and NPC (+4 Str, -4 Wis); racial feats: canny defense, darkvision; racial traits: open minded (x2); aberrant gifts: command undead, spell-like abilities.

Hooded HarbingerPF112 Cr 9

Advanced, variant tanar’ri aberrant paragon 2

CE Medium aberration [chaotic, evil, mythos]

Init +8; Senses darkvision 60 ft., planar sense 20 ft., see invisibility; Perception +21

Aura profane reek 5 ft. (see below; DC 21), unnatural aura

Languages Aklo, Common; telepathy 120 ft.

AC 25, touch 21, flat-footed 17

(+4 Dex, +4 dodge, +3 insight, +4 natural)

hp 161 (17 HD; LW 80/HW 40); DR 10/lawful

Immune negative energy, poison

Resist acid 10, cold 10, fire 10; SR 30

Fort +9, Ref +8, Int +7, Will +13; improved evasion, improved insight, improved resolve

Spd 30 ft.

Melee 2 slams +20 (1d4+12/19-20) or

bloodless touch +16 touch (see below)

Base Atk +12; CMB +26; CMD 40

Supernatural Abilities (ML 17th)

10/day—channel negative energy (1d6, DC 18)

Spell-Like Abilities (CL 17th)

1/day—extended freedom of movement, manifest Yellow Sign (see below; DC 22), plane shift, augmented (8d4) mass hold person (DC 24), terrible visage (see below; DC 25)

3/day—dispel magic, tongues, fiendish teleport*, confusion (DC 21), kindred summon monster IV (1 Advanced keeper of the Yellow Sign, 60%), prophetic utterance (see below)

At will—bloodless touch (see below; DC 18), detect law, hold person (DC 19), silence (DC 19)

Attributes Str 26, Dex 18, Con 21, Int 16, Wis 13, Cha 24

Feats Command UndeadB (56 CR), Deep Intuition, Dodge, Improved Critical, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Permanent Spell (aura), Weapon Finesse

Skills Acrobatics (17/+21), Athletics (17/+25), Bluff (17/+27), Concentration (17/+27), Escape Artist (17/+21), Knowledge (planes) (17/+23), Perception (17/+21), Planar Sense (17/+21), Stealth (17/+24)

Environment any land

Frequency very rare

Organization solitary (plus 1 possible Advanced Keeper of the Yellow Sign cohort and/or up to 50 CR worth of zombies)

Treasure standard

Bloodless Touch (Sp) Ray of entropy (1st level) + Cascade Spell (inertia; +1 level) + Augment Spell (staggered; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Cascade Spell (sickening touch; +1 level) + Lingering Evocation (+1 level) + Tenuous Spell (-1 level) + Restricted Spell (aberration; -1 level) + Reduce Spell (10d6 to 5d6; -1 level) = 1st level; melee touch deals 5d6 necrotic damage plus 2d6/rd. and staggered and sickened (save each round to end effects).

Death Throes (Sp) Bolt of force (2nd level) + Cascade Spell (alter senses; +1 level) + Augment Spell (blindness; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Shape Spell (target to burst; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r,; -1 level) = 4th level; damage cap 10d6 force plus blinded.

Manifest Yellow Sign (Sp) Ray of beguiling (1st level) + Cascade Spell (compel; +3 levels) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +2 levels) + Personal Spell (­1 level) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 120’r.; +3 levels) + Pattern Spell (visual; -1 level) + Restricted Spell (servant of Hastur; -1 level) = 5th level; onlookers within 120 ft. take a 1d6+15 penalty to Wisdom (confused at 1) and do not move or attempt to harm the caster in any way.

Profane Reek (Sp) Mind fog (5th level) + Reach Spell (long to touch; -2 levels) + Shape Spell (spread to emanation; +0 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.; -1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 hr./level; +2 levels) + Augment Spell (+10 to +15; +1 level) = 3rd level; those within 10 feet take a 1d6+15 penalty to Wis and Cha (Intuition half).

Prophetic Utterance (Sp) Doom (1st level) + Quickened Spell (+3 levels) + Interrupting Spell (+1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 10 min./level; +1 level) + Inexorable Spell (+3 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (just damaged caster; -2 levels) + Restricted Spell (aberration; -1 level) + Reduce Spell (panicked to shaken; -2 levels) = 4th level; as an immediate action, a hooded harbinger can cause a creature damaging it to be shaken for 170 min. (no save).

Terrible Visage (Sp) Damage attribute (Wis; 1st level) + Crippling Drain (+1 level) + Delay Spell (+1 level) + Pattern Spell (visual; -1 level) + Augment Spell (+2d4; +3 levels) + Cascade Spell [(bolt of force; +2 levels) + Cascade Spell (alter senses; +1 level) + Augment Spell (blindness; +1 level) + Reach Spell (close to personal; -1 level)] + Shape Spell (target to burst; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.; -1 level) + Delay Spell (+1 level) + Reduce Spell (25d6 to 15d6; -2 levels) = 8th level; onlookers of face (after slain) take 3d4 Wis drain, then body explodes for 15d6 force plus blinded in a 10’r. burst.

It is said that the Crawling Chaos is the messenger of the Great Old Ones, but whether this is by their command or his own whim is debatable. Regardless of why, the Great Old One known as Hastur sometimes instead relies on his hooded harbingers to relay messages to his far-flung cults and even to the High Priest Not To Be Described of mystery-shrouded Leng. These dread figures swathed in filthy yellow rags bear the whispered tidings of their Unnamed Lord. There are those who even speculate that the veiled priest of Leng is actually the greatest of the hooded harbingers, who gained some measure of autonomy—but the truth of this remains unknown. Thought to have originated in distant Carcosa by unthinkable means, hooded harbingers are exceedingly rare, and seldom is more than one encountered at a time.

Though tasked with the menial role of messengers, hooded harbingers take their charge very seriously. Infused with the hateful potency of their master, they are able to call upon many terrible powers in defense of their duties. When forced into combat, they prefer to trip opponents with the trailing ends of their ragged arm coverings and administer their bloodless touch to as many victims as possible. They always attempt to use plane shift to flee if in danger of imminent defeat.

Serving as messengers for Hastur, hooded harbingers receive the communications they deliver directly from the Great Old One via mental transmission. Upon receiving the message, the hooded harbinger twitches and shakes as if it were having a seizure. During this time they are particularly dangerous, because if they are attacked or distracted in any way, they fly into a furious rage and the offender risks attracting the attention of the King in Yellow.

Conversion Notes: attribute array: tanar’ri (+4 Str, +4 Dex, +4 Con, +2 Int, +2 Wis, +2 Cha), elite (+4 Str, +0 Dex, +2 Con, +0 Int, +0 Wis, +3 Cha), and NPC (+4 Str, -4 Wis); racial feats: canny defense, darkvision; racial traits: open minded (x2); aberrant gifts: command undead, spell-like abilities.

sections.heading: Hound of Tindalos
sections.text:
“They move slowly through angles. They have no bodies, and they move slowly through outrageous angles... God, they are breaking through! They are breaking through! Smoke is pouring in from the corners of the wall. Their tongues—ahhh—"
―Frank Belknap Long,
“The Hounds Of Tindalos” (1929)
All the evil in the universe is seemingly concentrated into this creature’s lean and hungry body. Many-jointed limbs extend from its gaunt, quadrupedal form, each ending in numerous twitching, clawed digits. From between the pallid flesh of its grasping forelimbs protrudes an alien face warped in a perpetual scream, a starved-looking visage where wide, depthless black eyes yawn above a fleshless, shuddering maw. A sharply pointed tongue projects from between its shattered teeth, quivering perversely.
Hound of TindalosPB2 	Cr 8
Advanced, half-fiend aberrant paragon 2/outsider 8
NE Medium outsider [evil]
Init +11; Senses darkvision 60 ft., planar sense 40 ft.; Perception +19
Aura ripping gaze 20 ft. (see below; DC 19)
Languages Aklo
AC 23, touch 17, flat-footed 16 (+7 Dex, +8 natural)
hp 95 (10 HD; LW 47/HW 23); DR 10/cold iron
Immune [mind-affecting], poison
Fort +8, Ref +13, Int +12, Will +10
Spd 40 ft., fly 40 ft.
Melee tongue +17 (2d4+7) and 2 claws +12 (1d4+3)
Base Atk +10; CMB +17; CMD 20
Special Atks smite 1/day (+4/+10)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th)
1/day—haste/slow (DC 17), dimensional anchor, plane shift (self, into angle or corner only)
3/day—invisibility
At will—reach dimensional skip (self, into angle or corner only)
Attributes Str 17, Dex 25, Con 18, Int 18, WIs 22, Cha 18
Feats Careful Speaker, Dimensional Agility, Improved Initiative, Permanent Spell (gaze), SkirmishB, Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics (10/+20), Athletics (10/+16), Bluff (10/+17), Concentration (10/+17), Knowledge (planes) (10/+17), Perception (10/+19), Planar Sense (10/+19), Stealth (10/+20)
Environment any (between planes)
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary or pack (2–13)
Treasure none

Ripping Gaze (Su) Invocation of the knife (0 level) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Shape Spell (ray to emanation; +2 levels) + Personal Spell (-1 level) + Extend Spell (inst. to 1 hr./level; +5 level) + Pattern Spell (visual; -1 level) + Reduce Spell (15d6 to 10d6; -1 level) = 4th level; damage cap 10d6 slashing/rd. (Reflex half) to those within 20 ft. The gaze of the hound tears the fabric of matter, destroying flesh at a distance and leaving deep, bloodless rents.
Hounds of Tindalos are otherworldly predators from beyond the bounds of known reality, usually appearing only when summoned by reckless spellcasters. They enter the physical world on their own in pursuit of those who have trodden too much the netherways beyond time and reality—time travelers (be it physical travel or simply divinatory glimpses forward or backward in time) and creatures that teleport without regard to how this movement impacts subtle magical currents in the multiverse particularly draw their interest.
What beings it can’t overwhelm with its slashing claws, siphoning tongue, and ripping gaze, a hound of Tindalos wears down with hit-and-run teleporting attacks. A wounded hound of Tindalos teleports away. The beast never forgets a victim, though, and will return to attack again and again until destroyed.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+0 Str, +4 Dex, +2 Con, +2 Int, +3 Wis, -2 Cha; racial modifiers +2 Dex, -2 Int, +2 Cha); racial feats: darkvision, feat mastery (Careful Speaker); racial traits: fast, improved natural attack (tongue); aberrant gifts: gaze, pounce. For a much weaker versionCoC, reduce outsider HD by 6 and remove the Advanced template (CR 4).

sections.heading: Larva of the Outer Gods
sections.text:
[O]utside the ordered universe [is] that amorphous blight of nethermost confusion which blasphemes and bubbles at the center of all infinity—the boundless daemon sultan Azathoth, whose name no lips dare speak aloud, and who gnaws hungrily in inconceivable, unlighted chambers beyond time and space amidst the muffled, maddening beating of vile drums and the thin monotonous whine of accursed flutes.
—H. P. Lovecraft,
The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath (1927)
This creature is a terrifying amalgamation of chitinous scales, bloated flesh, unblinking eyes, and writhing tentacles. Larvae of the Outer Gods are constantly shifting in form, but average 10 feet in diameter and weigh 1,600 pounds.
Larva of the Outer GodsPF114	Cr 12
Giant, half-farspawnLoM, obah-blessedDu136
aberrant paragon 3
CN Large aberration [mythos]
Init +12; Senses blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +17
Languages Aklo; telepathy 10 ft.
AC 31, touch 23, flat-footed 23
(-1 size, +8 Dex, +6 insight, +8 natural)
hp 200 (18 HD; LW 100/HW 50); DR 10/lawful
Immune poison; Resist acid 10, electricity 10; SR 32
Fort +12, Ref +14, Int +10, Will +14
Spd 20 ft., fly 60 ft.; starflight
Melee 8 tentacles +20 (1d6+13 plus poison)
Ranged sound lance +14/+9/+9 touch (6d6 sonic)
Face 5 ft. x 5 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Base Atk +13; CMB +24; CMD 40
Special Atks poison (tentacle—injury DC 25, 1d4 Dex and 1d4 Wis drain/rd., cure 2 saves)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 18th)
1/day—teleport, plane shift, liberate flesh (see below; DC 23), widened (60’r.) song of discordCRB (DC 24), mass effect irresistible dance (6 creatures; DC 25)
3/day—dimensional anchor
At will—summon instrument, split sound lance, magic circle against law
Attributes Str 20, Dex 26, Con 23, Int 11, Wis 14, Cha 22
Feats Agility Training, Canny Defense, Crippling Drain (poison) x2, Improved GrappleB, Improved Initiative, Toughness, Virulent Venom (x2), Weapon Finesse

Skills Acrobatics (18/+25), Concentration (18/+27), Fly (9/+19), Knowledge (planes) (15/+18), Perception (12/+17), Perform (music) (18/+24), Spellcraft (18/+21)
Environment any
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary, pair, or choir (4–6)
Treasure NPC gear (mojo 18,900; max. 21,000): up to 18 chaos beast victims
Liberate Flesh (Sp) Polymorph (outsider; 3rd level) + Reach Spell (touch to close; +1 level) + Extend Spell (1 min./level to 1 hr./level; +2 levels) + Mass Effect Spell (1 creature/3 levels; +2 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (under irresistible dance effect; -2 levels) + Accursed Spell (+1 level) = 7th level; up to 1 subject/3 levels is polymorphed into a chaos beast. The larva can invest 6,300 numen to make the effect permanent.
Void Singer (Su) The music of a larva of the Outer Gods travels through the fabric of reality itself. Sonic spells and effects produced by the larva, including its maddening song and liberated flesh abilities, function even in the void of space, in areas of magical silence, and against deaf creatures. A larva of the Outer Gods does not breathe, and is immune to the effects of vacuum.

At the heart of the Dark Tapestry lies Azathoth, a shapeless entity the size of a star, imbued with immense chaotic and destructive power. The members of Azathoth’s court orbit it like planets, exalting in the babbling nonsense the blind idiot god issues into the void and singing songs of exquisite madness to their lord. The least of this celestial choir are the larvae of the Outer Gods, shed from Azathoth as a body sheds skin cells. They conjure instruments from the ether, such as pipes and flutes, with which to serenade their progenitor as they mature into gods of the void.
Foolish mortals sometimes call upon the larvae of the Outer Gods for aid, summoning them to the realms of men in order to strike down some mortal enemy or share the forbidden secrets of Azathoth. While larvae are not opposed to serving such mortals, they also care little for what effect their songs have on mortal flesh. Those who conjure a larva of the Outer Gods are just as likely to fall victim to its maddening song as those they hoped to smite, and those who seek the secrets of the cosmos often learn them at the cost of their corporeal forms. Even when summoners take steps to protect themselves from unwelcome transformations, they find that the larvae of the Outer Gods approach tasks with an unfocused dreaminess that makes them terrible servants.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: half-farspawn (+2 Str, +2 Dex, +6 Con, +4 Wis, +2 Cha) and elite (+2 Str, +4 Dex, +0 Con, +0 Int, +0 Wis, +3 Cha); racial feats: darkvision, flight; racial traits: open minded (x2); aberrant gifts: poison (x2), starflight, void singer.

sections.heading: Mi-Go
sections.text:
They were pinkish things about five feet long; with crustaceous bodies bearing vast pairs of dorsal fins or membranous wings and several sets of articulated limbs, and with a sort of convoluted ellipsoid, covered with multitudes of very short antennae, where a head would normally be.	―H.P. Lovecraft,
“The Whisperer in Darkness” (1930)
Mi-GoPB4	Cr 6
Half-advanced, awakened, wingedSS plant creature 3
NE Medium aberration [mythos, fungus, plant]
Init +4; Senses low-light vision, tremorsense 30 ft.; Perception +14
Aura unnatural aura
Languages Mi-Go, Aklo, Common, +4 others
AC 25, touch 20, flat-footed 21
(+4 Dex, +6 insight, +5 natural)
hp 76 (9 HD; LW 38/HW 19);
DR 5/slashing or bludgeoning
Immune cold; plant traits; Resist electric 5, fire 5
Fort +5, Ref +3, Int +5, Will +3
Weaknesses light sensitivity, vulnerability to sonics
Spd 30 ft., fly 50 ft.; starflight
Melee 2 claws +10 (1d4+4 plus grab)
Base Atk +6; CMB +10 (grapple +13); CMD 21
Special Atks constrict (2d6+4 plus 1d6 attribute damage)
Attributes Str 12, Dex 18, Con 19, Int 22, Wis 14, Cha 15
Feats Canny Defense, Concussive Strike, Crippling Strike, Imbue Item, Improved GrappleB, Vital StrikeB, Weapon Finesse
Skills Bluff (9/+11), Craft (bio-electromechanical device) (9/+15), Disable Device (9/+15), EnduranceB (3/+10), FlyB (9/+17), Heal (9/+11), Knowledge (planes) (9/+15), Perception (9/+14), Perform (acting) (9/+11), Spellcraft (9/+15), Stealth (9/+17)
Environment temperate hills and mountains (Yuggoth)
Frequency very rare
Organization scouting party (2–8) or invasion (9–16)
Treasure double standard
Starflight (Su) A mi-go can survive in the void of outer space. It flies through space at incredible speeds. Although exact travel times vary, a trip within a single solar system normally takes 3d20 months, while a trip beyond normally takes 3d20 years (or more)—provided the mi-go knows the way to its destination.

Mi-go (“The Fungi from Yuggoth”) are both scientists and colonists—extraterrestrial travelers from deep space who view the universe as a canvas to be mastered and controlled. Their numbers on any particular planet can vary, but taken on a galactic scale, are mind-numbing in scope. Although a mi-go's shape might suggest it is an arthropod, the creature is in fact a highly evolved form of extraterrestrial fungus. Mi-go communicate via a combination of clicking pincers and subtle shifts in the coloration of their bulbous heads. A typical mi-go is roughly the size of a human, but weighs only 90 pounds.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+0 Str, +0 Dex, +2 Con, +4 Int, +0 Wis, +3 Cha) and NPC (-4 Str, +4 Int); racial traits: trade freeze for open minded, gain low-light vision at the expense of light sensitivity; verdant gifts: constrict, starflight, supple; accept vulnerability to gain immunity.

The bones of the tiny paws... imply prehensile characteristics more typical of a diminutive monkey than of a rat: while the small skull with its savage yellow fangs is of the utmost anomalousness, appearing from certain angles like a miniature, monstrously degraded parody of a human skull.

Rat-things are said to be created from dead cultists by foul witch craft. Thus, they are found where the witch who created them had her lair. As unnatural creatures, rat-things never die a natural death, although they can be killed. Hence a witch's familiar might still be found lurking in the walls of her domicile centuries after its mistress is ashes. (Brown Jenkin, Keziah Mason's familiar, was an unusually powerful rat-thing.) They are full of malice and mischief, and delight in tormenting hapless mortals, willingly serving any evil sorcerer powerful enough to master them.
Ratlings are carnivores. While they can subsist on grubs, other rodents, and carrion, they prefer living food and fresh blood, particularly that of humanoid children and elderly folk. They also have a sense for magic, and lurk around temples and universities searching for scraps of knowledge or overlooked books and scrolls to steal.

Tenuous Natural Invisibility (Su) This functions like natural invisibility, except it is subject to invisibility purge and effects that outline invisible creatures (such as glitterdust and faerie fire). It cannot be dispelled.
The spawn of Yog-Sothoth are begotten upon the world as the results of vile rituals in which cultists call down the essence of Yog-Sothoth, an Outer God from beyond the stars to impregnate a humanoid creature. The Outer God is not of this dimension or world; only by incorporating flesh and bone of a mortal can its spawn exist. Upon death, a spawn's flesh rapidly melts until nothing remains but a crusty stain. Although the spawn of Yog-Sothoth are naturally invisible, they exude a hideous, unforgettable stench that alerts others to their presence.
A spawn of Yog-Sothoth grows quickly to Large size, but if it continues to feed, it also continues to grow, albeit at a lesser rate. An ancient spawn of Yog-Sothoth can be the size of a barn or even a small hill. However, not all spawn of Yog-Sothoth are massive or inhuman. Some (often twins to their more monstrous kin) remain roughly humanoid in shape and size, although their deformities still require them to wear disguises or layers of baggy clothing if they want to walk unchallenged in civilized regions. These sinister creatures have a wide range of strange and unusual abilities and appearances, and are usually spellcasters—typically oracles with the dark tapestry mystery or sorcerers with the aberrant bloodline.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+4 Str, +0 Dex, -2 Con, +2 Int, +2 Wis, +3 Cha); racial feats: additional natural attack (bite), thick hide; racial traits: agile climber, open minded; aberrant gifts: stench, tenuous natural invisibility.

sections.heading: Star-Spawn
sections.text:
A mountainous form, this hideous creature is humanoid in general shape, but its hateful face is a writhing mass of tentacles. The star-spawn of Cthulhu have a strange, mutable anatomy—their form is not fixed. They can absorb parts of their bodies or enlarge others at will, a trait they often use on their claws or tentacles to dramatically extend their reach in combat beyond what might normally be possible for a creature of the same shape and size. Despite this mutable shape, the star-spawn’s forms generally don’t deviate far from that of an octopus-headed, winged humanoid, likely because of the powerful links their otherworldly minds have to their overlord and master, who lies dead but dreaming in the lost city of R’lyeh.

Overwhelming Mind (Su) Inertia (0 level) + Fell Inertia (+1 level) + Augment Spell (stunned; +3 levels) + Channel Spell (through mental contact; +1 level) + Creature-Specific Spell (not subject to this effect previously; -2 levels) + Quicken Spell (+3 levels) + Restricted Spell (Careful Speaker; -1 level) = 5th level; the first time a creature makes or receives mental contact with a star-spawn, the latter can, with a swift action, cause it to be stunned 1 round (Will dazed).
Of all the strange and malefic denizens of the void between the stars, few cause the same terror as this titanic race. They hail from a mad star whose light cannot be seen by conventional telescopes, and the smallest of these behemoths stand nearly 30 feet in height. Humanoid in shape, their immense bodies have rubbery flesh that seems to wriggle and seethe like a half-solidified ooze. Tremendous draconic wings, murderous taloned hands, and a tentacled visage that evokes the alien gaze of an octopus complete the being’s monstrous shape. This malevolent race has a name, yet it is no name known to the sane. Among mortal scholars, they are known merely by the name of their greatest priest—they are the star-spawn of Cthulhu.
The star-spawn of Cthulhu hold little malice toward indigenous life—they simply can’t proceed with their plans for a world while such life exists. Just as a human might move into a house thinking it to be abandoned, only to discover colonies of ants dwelling within the building’s walls, the star-spawn work to eradicate indigenous infestations. Their methods seldom vary from world to world—those whose intellects they can influence via dreams and nightmares they besiege as the victims sleep, seeding the growth of destructive cults and societies. These groups in turn further the star-spawn’s agenda, preparing the world and bringing it to the brink of destruction. When such worlds are poised to tear themselves apart from within through unrest, civil war, excessive pollution, or genocide, the star-spawn mobilize their cults to end all things. The only reward such cults may receive for their (sometimes unwitting) aid is the dubious honor of being among the final few to be eradicated, for the star-spawn have no interest in and feel no responsibility toward their pawns.

One star-spawn is a demigod-tier threat, and a cult of them is nearly equivalent to a lesser god. The fact that the star-spawns’ plans to bring about the eradication of life take centuries or even millennia should not be mistaken for sloth or lassitude—the star-spawn are inhumanly patient, and the preparation of the universe’s worlds must precisely follow an unknowable schedule, for only when the exact cosmic convergences are in place and the stars are right can they make their final moves to end all things. This time frame does give some worlds a chance to discover the star-spawns’ influence and to delay or even defeat their world’s doom, but such tales of triumph are rare in the face of the void’s relentless tides.

Star-Spawn

A mountainous form, this hideous creature is humanoid in general shape, but its hateful face is a writhing mass of tentacles. The star-spawn of Cthulhu have a strange, mutable anatomy—their form is not fixed. They can absorb parts of their bodies or enlarge others at will, a trait they often use on their claws or tentacles to dramatically extend their reach in combat beyond what might normally be possible for a creature of the same shape and size. Despite this mutable shape, the star-spawn’s forms generally don’t deviate far from that of an octopus-headed, winged humanoid, likely because of the powerful links their otherworldly minds have to their overlord and master, who lies dead but dreaming in the lost city of R’lyeh.

Of all the strange and malefic denizens of the void between the stars, few cause the same terror as this titanic race. They hail from a mad star whose light cannot be seen by conventional telescopes, and the smallest of these behemoths stand nearly 30 feet in height. Humanoid in shape, their immense bodies have rubbery flesh that seems to wriggle and seethe like a half-solidified ooze. Tremendous draconic wings, murderous taloned hands, and a tentacled visage that evokes the alien gaze of an octopus complete the being’s monstrous shape. This malevolent race has a name, yet it is no name known to the sane. Among mortal scholars, they are known merely by the name of their greatest priest—they are the star-spawn of Cthulhu.

The Tcho-Tcho are the last remnants of an exceedingly ancient people. Although they can pass for small humans thanks to their Veiled Vileness trait, they appear to be of no known human ethnicity. Darker than most of their Asian neighbors, they arc infamous among the few who have heard of them for an extremely primitive culture, vicious religious practices (including human sacrifice), and unsavory culinary practices (such as cannibalism).

A living and corporeal creature bitten by a thought eater (including via Ghost Strike) loses some of its thoughts, as the thought eater drains them to nourish itself. If the victim is a spellcaster, she loses a single spell prepared, or a single unused spell slot (if she is a spontaneous spellcaster) of 1st level or higher. A spellcaster chooses which spell or spell slot she loses from this ability. If the victim is not a spellcaster or has no prepared spells or unused spell slots of 1st level or higher, on a failed saving throw this ability instead deals 1 point of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma damage (victim's choice).

These tiny predators of thought live almost their entire lives on the Ethereal Plane. They are so tied to that place that without its energy, a thought eater's psychic power begins to deplete, until finally the very fabric of its own personal reality breaks down and it fades out of existence. But while the Ethereal Plane is necessary for thought eaters' continued existence, its vastness and relative lack of prey force thought eaters to sometimes hunt on the Material Plane. Such trips are often gluttonous affairs, as the thought eaters must not only gain sustenance, but also gain enough nourishment to stave off their rapid psychic and physical decay in that hostile environment.
Normally, thought eaters are fairly single-minded, but the inherent danger in their forays to the Material Plane makes them eager for easy meals. Someone who takes the time to provide consistent easy meals for a thought eater can expect the creature to follow her on the Ethereal Plane, watching for its next feeding time. Given that every minute on the Material Plane is strenuous for a thought eater, such a person is unlikely to receive much conversation from the creature trailing her, but if something threatens the safety of its food source, the thought eater may be moved to protect its companion. In this case, the thought eater uses its daze monster ability to help the person escape. If this bizarre and alien friendship continues for long enough, the thought eater may even choose to assist in identifying magic items—when properly compensated, of course.

Towering over normal-sized creatures, this monster has transparent skin that seems to flow away from its body, allowing glimpses of its internal organs and bones. Glowing eyes peer out from an avian head, topping a notably feline form.
Fully-grown forms of thought eaters, thought slayers also survive by consuming the mental energy of intelligent creatures, but they are far deadlier than their lesser cousins. Like the thought eater, thought slayers are able to quickly travel to and from the Material Plane from the Ethereal Plane, and like thought eaters, thought slayers do not speak.
Thought slayer tactics revolve around waiting in the Ethereal Plane for intelligent, or preferably psionic, creatures to come near. It will then shift to the Material Plane in an attempt to ambush its intended victim. If this ambush proves successful, the thought slayer returns back to the Ethereal Plane to digest its newly acquired meal.

Brain moles who gorge themselves on psychic energy occasionally find their bodies wracked by magically infused tumors that vastly enhance their intellects and psychic spellcasting but condemn the moles to slow deaths. Most then use their newfound mental abilities to attempt to secure a legacy or to provide for their nests once they pass on, and their mad plots become increasingly eccentric and aggressive as the end nears.

A nimbus of glowing, intangible matter envelops this strange skeletal creature with a bird-like beak.

A living and corporeal creature bitten by a thought eater (including via Ghost Strike) loses some of its thoughts, as the thought eater drains them to nourish itself. If the victim is a spellcaster, she loses a single spell prepared, or a single unused spell slot (if she is a spontaneous spellcaster) of 1st level or higher. A spellcaster chooses which spell or spell slot she loses from this ability. If the victim is not a spellcaster or has no prepared spells or unused spell slots of 1st level or higher, on a failed saving throw this ability instead deals 1 point of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma damage (victim's choice).

These tiny predators of thought live almost their entire lives on the Ethereal Plane. They are so tied to that place that without its energy, a thought eater's psychic power begins to deplete, until finally the very fabric of its own personal reality breaks down and it fades out of existence. But while the Ethereal Plane is necessary for thought eaters' continued existence, its vastness and relative lack of prey force thought eaters to sometimes hunt on the Material Plane. Such trips are often gluttonous affairs, as the thought eaters must not only gain sustenance, but also gain enough nourishment to stave off their rapid psychic and physical decay in that hostile environment.

Normally, thought eaters are fairly single-minded, but the inherent danger in their forays to the Material Plane makes them eager for easy meals. Someone who takes the time to provide consistent easy meals for a thought eater can expect the creature to follow her on the Ethereal Plane, watching for its next feeding time. Given that every minute on the Material Plane is strenuous for a thought eater, such a person is unlikely to receive much conversation from the creature trailing her, but if something threatens the safety of its food source, the thought eater may be moved to protect its companion. In this case, the thought eater uses its daze monster ability to help the person escape. If this bizarre and alien friendship continues for long enough, the thought eater may even choose to assist in identifying magic items—when properly compensated, of course.

Each round after the first, the thought slayer can target another creature as a partial action.

Towering over normal-sized creatures, this monster has transparent skin that seems to flow away from its body, allowing glimpses of its internal organs and bones. Glowing eyes peer out from an avian head, topping a notably feline form.

Fully-grown forms of thought eaters, thought slayers also survive by consuming the mental energy of intelligent creatures, but they are far deadlier than their lesser cousins. Like the thought eater, thought slayers are able to quickly travel to and from the Material Plane from the Ethereal Plane, and like thought eaters, thought slayers do not speak.

Thought slayer tactics revolve around waiting in the Ethereal Plane for intelligent, or preferably psionic, creatures to come near. It will then shift to the Material Plane in an attempt to ambush its intended victim. If this ambush proves successful, the thought slayer returns back to the Ethereal Plane to digest its newly acquired meal.

sections.heading: Intellect Devourer
sections.text:
“I have been with the Palesedran authorizes all morning and they have, I believe, discovered the source of Finnerack’s odd behavior.”
With deftness and delicacy the Palesedrans extracted a white sac the size of two clenched fists...  suddenly it evinced a squirming life of its own. The white sac burst away; out crawled a glossy brown creature, something between a spider and a crab.
“There you see your true enemy,” said Ifness. “Its intelligence appears to be of the highest order.”
The creature was gnarled and convoluted like a small brown brain; six jointed legs left the underside of the body, each ending in three strong palps.
“From my brief acquaintance with the asutra,” said Ifness, “I deduce it to be a parasite; or better yet perhaps, the directive half of a symbiosis...”
―Jack Vance, The Brave Free Men (1972)

Thought by some to be invaders from another dimension or planet, the sinister intellect devourers are certainly one of the world's cruelest races. Incapable of experiencing emotions or wallowing in the sins of physical pleasure on their own, intellect devourers are forced to steal bodies in order to indulge their gluttony, lust, and cruelty. Stories tell of entire cities of these creatures deep underground, where host bodies are worn like clothes to hideous orgies and vile feasts. Lone intellect devourers often dwell in ruins or caves on the edge of a civilized region so they can make periodic forays into town to “shop” for an attractive new body.

Half-fiend aberrant paragon 4
CE Small aberration [evil, outsider]
Init +9; Senses blindsight 60 ft., Planar Sense 10 ft.; Perception +14
Languages Undercommon (can’t speak)
AC 20, touch 16, flat-footed 15
(+1 size, +5 Dex, +4 natural)
hp 69 (7 HD; LW 34/HW 17); DR 10/adamantine
Immune fire, [mind-affecting]
Resist cold 10, electricity 10, sonic 10; SR 24
Fort +7, Ref +8, Int +6, Will +9
Weaknesses vulnerability to protection from evil
Spd 30 ft., climb 30 ft.
Melee 3 claws +11 (1d3+1)
Base Atk +5; CMB +9; CMD 20

Special Atks sneak attack +3d6
Supernatural Abilties (ML 7th)
1/day—body thief (DC 17; see below)
Psi-Like Abilities (ML 7th)
1/day—detect thoughts (DC 16), confusion (DC 17), globe of invulnerability
At will—daze person (DC 14), detect magic, reduce self
Attributes Str 12, Dex 21, Con 18, Int 12, Wis 12, Cha 18
Feats Improved Initiative, Natural Spell, Toughness, Weapon Finesse
Skills Athletics (7/+11; climb +14), Bluff (7/+17), Concentration (7/+17), Perception (7/+14), Perform (acting) (7/+14), Planar Sense (7/+11), Stealth (7/+22)
Environment any underground
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary or pod (2–4)
Treasure half coins, double goods, standard objects
Body Thief (Su) PossessionOcA (3rd level) + Cascade Spell [(detection: memories; +3 levels) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level)] + Accursed Spell (+1 level) + Creature-Restricted Spell (helpless or dead; -2 levels) + Ritual Spell (full round; -1 level) = 4th level. The half-fiend template provides the non-native outsider clause of the possession seed to apply; it appears as if the intellect devourer is shrinking itself, crawling into the host’s mouth, and taking up residence in its head. Damage done to a host body does not harm the intellect devourer, and if the host body is slain, the intellect devourer emerges and is dazed for 1 round.
Vulnerable to Protection from Evil (Ex) An intellect devourer is treated as a summoned creature for the purpose of determining how it is affected by a protection from evil spell.

sections.heading: Mind Flayer
sections.text:
This strange humanoid-shaped being stands about as tall as a human. Its flesh is rubbery and greenish-mauve, glistening with slime. The creature’s head looks like a four-tentacled octopus with a pair of bloated white eyes. Mind flayers, also called illithids, are so insidious and powerful that all denizens of the dark fear them. They bend others to their will and shatter enemies’ minds. A mind flayer’s mouth, a revolting thing shaped like a lamprey’s maw, constantly drips an oily slime when it is not siphoning out the brains of living prey.
Mind FlayerMM	Cr 6
Half-farspawnLoM aberrant paragon 3
LE Medium aberration [evil]
Init +6; Senses blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +15
Languages Aklo, Common, Mabrahoring, R’lyehian, Undercommon; telepathy 40 ft.
AC 22, touch 16, flat-footed 20
(+2 Dex, +4 insight, +6 natural)
hp 58 (9 HD; LW 29/HW 14); DR 5/magic
Immune poison
Resist acid 10, electricity 10; SR 23
Fort +5, Ref +5, Int +8, Will +8
Spd 30 ft.
Melee 4 tentacles +12 (1d4+6 plus grab)
Base Atk +6; CMB +7 (grapple +13); CMD 19
Special Atks extract brain
Supernatural Ability (ML 9th)
1/day—mind blast (see below; DC 18)
Psi-Like Abilities (ML 9th)
1/day—suggestion (DC 16), charm monster (DC 17), personal plane shift
3/day—detect thoughts (DC 15)
At will—levitate
Attributes Str 12, Dex 14, Con 14, Int 19, Wis 17, Cha 16

Skills Bluff (9/+15), Concentration (9/+19), Diplomacy (9/+12), Knowledge (lore, the planes) (9/+16), Perception (9/+15), Spellcraft (9/+13), Stealth (9/+14)
Environment underground
Frequency rare
Organization solitary, pair, inquisition (3–5), or cult (3–5 plus 6–10 grimlocks)
Treasure NPC gear

Extract Brain (Ex) As the Killing Stroke feat, but each tentacle attached after the first counts as an additional round (a mind flayer grappling a creature with all four tentacles can make a coup de grâce attempt on a pin; if successful, the victim’s brain is extracted, killing it). A mind flayer can attempt to extract a stunned opponent’s brain as a standard action.
Mind Blast (Su) Inertia (0 level) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Shape Spell (target to cone; +1 level) + Widen Spell (30 ft. to 60 ft.; +1 level) + Augment Spell (stunned; +3 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd. to 1 rd./level; +1 level) + Tenuous Spell (-1 level) + Restricted Spell (psionic; -1 level) = 5th level; those in 60-ft. cone are stunned 1 rd./level or until save.
Mind flayers like to fight from a distance, using their psionic abilities, particularly mind blast. Mind flayers often hunt using this power, and then drag off one or two of their stunned victims to feed upon. If pressed into melee combat, a mind flayer lashes its enemies with the tentacles ringing its mouth.
In addition to being highly intelligent, wholly evil, and terribly sadistic, mind flayers are utterly self-serving. If an encounter turns against the creature, it flees at once, caring nothing for the fate of its companions or servitors.

sections.heading: Grimlock
sections.text:
Slaves to the mind flayers, grimlocks are powerfully-built humanoids clad only in dark, filthy rags. These warlike subterranean creatures emerge from their deep caverns at night to search for unlucky humans to add to their larders. Grimlocks have thick, scaly, grey skin and long, black, filthy hair. Their teeth are white and extremely sharp. Their eyes are blank white orbs.

Monstrous humanoid 2
NE Medium monstrous humanoid
Init +1; Senses blind; blindsight 30 ft., scent; Perception +8
Languages Undercommon
AC 14, touch 11, flat-footed 13 (+1 Dex, +3 natural)
hp 15 (2 HD; LW 7/HW 3)
Immune visual effects
Fort +4, Ref +5, Int +3, Will +3
Spd 30 ft.; tunnel runner
Melee battleaxe +4 (1d8+3/×3) or
Power Attack +3 (1d8+6/x3)
Base Atk +2; CMB +4; CMD 15

SQ favored terrain (underground) +2
Feats Power Attack
Skills Athletics (1/+6), Profession (mining) (1/+7), Perception (1/+8), Stealth (1/+8; +10 underground)
Environment underground
Frequency uncommon
Organization gang (2-4), pack (10-20), tribe (10-60 plus 1 leader of 3rd-5th level per 10 adults).
Treasure standard coins; standard goods (gems only); standard items (stone battleaxe, other)

Grimlocks are blind, but their exceptional senses of smell and hearing allow them to notice foes nearby. As a result, they usually shun ranged weapons and rush to the attack, brandishing their stone battleaxes. Grimlocks are susceptible to sound- and scent-based attacks, however, and are affected normally by loud noises and sonic spells (such as ghost sound or silence) and overpowering odors (such as stinking cloud or incense-heavy air). Negating a grimlock’s sense of smell or hearing reduces this ability to normal Blind-Fight (as the feat). If both these senses are negated, a grimlock is effectively blinded.

html:
Mind Flayer

This strange humanoid-shaped being stands about as tall as a human. Its flesh is rubbery and greenish-mauve, glistening with slime. The creature’s head looks like a four-tentacled octopus with a pair of bloated white eyes. Mind flayers, also called illithids, are so insidious and powerful that all denizens of the dark fear them. They bend others to their will and shatter enemies’ minds. A mind flayer’s mouth, a revolting thing shaped like a lamprey’s maw, constantly drips an oily slime when it is not siphoning out the brains of living prey.

Mind FlayerMM Cr 6

Half-farspawnLoM aberrant paragon 3

LE Medium aberration [evil]

Init +6; Senses blindsight 60 ft., darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +15

Languages Aklo, Common, Mabrahoring, R’lyehian, Undercommon; telepathy 40 ft.

AC 22, touch 16, flat-footed 20

(+2 Dex, +4 insight, +6 natural)

hp 58 (9 HD; LW 29/HW 14); DR 5/magic

Immune poison

Resist acid 10, electricity 10; SR 23

Fort +5, Ref +5, Int +8, Will +8

Spd 30 ft.

Melee 4 tentacles +12 (1d4+6 plus grab)

Base Atk +6; CMB +7 (grapple +13); CMD 19

Special Atks extract brain

Supernatural Ability (ML 9th)

1/day—mind blast (see below; DC 18)

Psi-Like Abilities (ML 9th)

1/day—suggestion (DC 16), charm monster (DC 17), personal plane shift

3/day—detect thoughts (DC 15)

At will—levitate

Attributes Str 12, Dex 14, Con 14, Int 19, Wis 17, Cha 16

Feats Canny Defense, Improved GrappleB, Improved Initiative, Permanent Spell (extended personal divine favor), Weapon Specialization (tentacles)

Skills Bluff (9/+15), Concentration (9/+19), Diplomacy (9/+12), Knowledge (lore, the planes) (9/+16), Perception (9/+15), Spellcraft (9/+13), Stealth (9/+14)

Environment underground

Frequency rare

Organization solitary, pair, inquisition (3–5), or cult (3–5 plus 6–10 grimlocks)

Treasure NPC gear

Extract Brain (Ex) As the Killing Stroke feat, but each tentacle attached after the first counts as an additional round (a mind flayer grappling a creature with all four tentacles can make a coup de grâce attempt on a pin; if successful, the victim’s brain is extracted, killing it). A mind flayer can attempt to extract a stunned opponent’s brain as a standard action.

Mind Blast (Su) Inertia (0 level) + Still Spell (+1 level) + Shape Spell (target to cone; +1 level) + Widen Spell (30 ft. to 60 ft.; +1 level) + Augment Spell (stunned; +3 levels) + Extend Spell (1 rd. to 1 rd./level; +1 level) + Tenuous Spell (-1 level) + Restricted Spell (psionic; -1 level) = 5th level; those in 60-ft. cone are stunned 1 rd./level or until save.

Mind flayers like to fight from a distance, using their psionic abilities, particularly mind blast. Mind flayers often hunt using this power, and then drag off one or two of their stunned victims to feed upon. If pressed into melee combat, a mind flayer lashes its enemies with the tentacles ringing its mouth.

In addition to being highly intelligent, wholly evil, and terribly sadistic, mind flayers are utterly self-serving. If an encounter turns against the creature, it flees at once, caring nothing for the fate of its companions or servitors.

Slaves to the mind flayers, grimlocks are powerfully-built humanoids clad only in dark, filthy rags. These warlike subterranean creatures emerge from their deep caverns at night to search for unlucky humans to add to their larders. Grimlocks have thick, scaly, grey skin and long, black, filthy hair. To create a neothelid, not only must an illithid (Mind Flayer, q.v.) tadpole not undergo ceremorphosis, but the elder brain of the colony must be absent, as the elder brain would normally eat all tadpoles that failed to undergo ceremorphosis. Somalcygots are incredibly territorial; each claims roughly a mile-radius patch of desolate surface on a moon, asteroid, or similar airless terrestrial environment as its chosen hunting ground. Somalcygots can digest nearly any organic matter, but because they usually live on barren terrain, they often go for long intervals without a meal. In order to preserve energy between meals, a somalcygot enters a trance-like hibernation during which it burrows in circles beneath the surface of its territory.
When it detects another creature nearby, the somalcygot awakens and enters a frenzy to capitalize on the rare meal, fighting relentlessly until the prey either dies or escapes. Only rarely do somalcygots pursue prey beyond the boundaries of their claimed hunting grounds, a tendency that serves both to preserve the creature's energy and to avoid needless conflict with other somalcygots that claim neighboring regions.

sections.heading: Balhannoth
sections.text:
A hulking creature with an ovoid body drops from the ceiling. It moves on six long tentacles instead of legs, and from between its shoulders protrudes a slavering mouth full of jagged, ripping teeth. A typical balhannoth stands approximately 9 feet tall at the shoulder and weighs about 2 tons.
BalhannothMM4 	Cr 9
Giant, advanced animal paragon 1/
aberrant paragon 4
CN Large aberration
Init +7; Senses blind, dweomersight 60 ft.; Perception +12
Aura dimensional lock 20 ft. (DC 21)
AC 16, touch 12, flat-footed 18
(-1 size, +3 Dex, +9 natural)
hp 39 (14 HD; LW 19/HW 9); DR 15/magic
Immune visual effects; Resist SR 25
Fort +12, Ref +9, Int +8, Will +8
Spd 50 ft., climb 50 ft.
Melee 2 slams +18 (1d6+9 plus grab) and
bite +13 (1d8+4)
Face 5 ft. x 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft. (lunge 10 ft.)
Base Atk +10; CMB +20 (grapple +24); CMD 33
Special Atks constrict (2d6+13 plus greater dispel magic)
Attributes Str 29, Dex 17, Con 23, Int 3, Wis 14,   Cha 15
Feats Dispelling Strike, Feat Mastery (dispelling strike), Improved GrappleB, Improved Initiative, Lunge, Permanent Spell (dimensional lock aura), Prana Practitioner, Vital StrikeB +1
Skills Athletics (7/+19; climb +11), Concentration (14/+23), Perception (7/+12), Stealth (14/+16)
Environment underground
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary or brood (2–6)
Treasure half monetary plus NPC gear (magic items)
Dimensional Lock Aura (Sp) Dimensional lock (7th level) – Reach Spell (-1 level) + Personal Spell (-1 level) = 5th level.
Dweomersight (Sp) Detection (magic; 2nd level) + Extend Spell (conc. to 1 min./level; +4 levels) + Restricted Spell (-1 level) = 5th level; a balhannoth “sees” nearby magical auras.

Horrid aberrations of the subterranean realm, balhannoths hunt by tracking magical energy. They can “see” magic but are otherwise blind. Nothing magical functions in their powerful grips, making these predators especially deadly to those who rely on spells or magic items.
Balhannoths feed on both flesh and magical auras. A magic item with a faint aura sustains a balhannoth for a day, one with a moderate aura gives food for a week, and one with a strong aura is sufficient for a month. How long a balhannoth might survive on an overwhelming magical aura is unknown, but some scholars believe an item of such power might sustain it for life. A balhannoth enjoys the taste of magic but does no permanent harm to an item. Eventually it tires of the magic’s flavor and must seek out a new source
of nourishment.
The strange feeding needs of balhannoths drive them to attack and kill magic-bearing individuals. The creatures can’t tell the difference between a magic item and an ongoing spell effect, so they attack anything they can detect with their dweomersight. A creature without magic is in no danger unless it enters the area of a balhannoth’s dimensional lock aura, rendering it “visible” to the predator.
Once a balhannoth has killed its prey and dealt with any other threats, it takes the corpse back to its lair. There it devours the flesh and separates out any magic items the creature possessed. It chooses one item to carry and feed on, placing the others in a hidden or hard-to-reach place. Common hiding places for such food stores include cavities beneath large boulders or cracks in cavern ceilings.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+3 Str, +2 Dex, +4 Con, +0 Int, -2 Wis, +2 Cha) and NPC (+4 Str, ­4 Con); racial feats: additional traits, thick hide; racial traits: agile climber, fast (x2), open minded; special attack: constrict; aberrant gifts: damage reduction, dweomersight, spell resistance.

sections.heading: Bonesucker
sections.text:
This bizarre creature resembles a fleshy tree trunk. Atop its main body protrudes a mass of writhing tentacles that constantly ooze and drip a brownish-yellow fluid. Near the top of its body is a ring of black, unblinking eyes. Bonesuckers stand about 10 feet tall.
BonesuckerToH 	Cr 5
Giant, obah-blessedDu136 aberrant paragon 2
NE Large aberration
Init +5; Senses alertness +3 (DC 30), darkvision 60 ft., uncanny dodge, improved uncanny dodge; Perception +16
Languages Aklo
AC 18, touch 12, flat-footed 15
(-1 size, +1 Dex, +2 dodge, +6 natural)
hp 60 (8 HD; LW 30/HW 15); DR 10/magic
Fort +5, Ref +3, Int +5, Will +5
Spd 20 ft.
Melee 4 tentacles +9 (1d6+4 plus grab)
Face 5 ft. x 5 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Base Atk +6; CMB +11 (grapple +14); CMD 25
Special Atks poison (tentacle—injury DC 17, 1d3 Str and 1d3 Dex/rd. for 6 rds., cure 2 saves)
Attributes Str 18, Dex 13, Con 17, Int 10, Wis 12,  Cha 12
Feats Alertness, Dodge, Improved GrappleB, Improved Initiative, +1
Skills Athletics (8/+11), Perception (8/+16), Stealth (8/+8), Survival (8/+12)
Environment any land and underground
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary
Treasure standard
A bonesucker is a bizarre creature that stalks the darkness of wastelands and dank caves. The body is encased in a thick, rubbery sheath of flesh and muscle that makes the bonesucker highly resistant to injury. The bonesucker moves about through the use of 5 thick tentacles at its base. Bonesuckers consume only the bones of an opponent by grabbing it and piercing its flesh with its hollow tentacles. The tentacles inject digestive enzymes into the bones, which break down and are sucked up as a pasty meal for the bonesucker—the attack of a bonesucker is horrifyingly painful. Experienced adventurers always know they are nearing the hunting grounds of a bonesucker: the creature leaves boneless carcasses of its meals lying where it finished them.

Conversion Notes: attribute array: elite (+3 Str, +4 Dex, +2 Con, -2 Int, +2 Wis, +0 Cha; racial +2 Int); racial feats: darkvision, thick hide; racial traits: skill focus (Perception), +1; aberrant gifts: poison (x2).
